section: Satavahana administration, economy, coinage and Prakrit literature (Hala's Gathasaptasati)
subsections: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors
Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins

accepted.s: Who among the following Satavahana rulers is associated with the authorship of Gathasaptasati (Sattasai)?
accepted.x: Gathasaptasati was composed under Hala, the seventeenth Satavahana king, who bore the title Kavivatsala.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–work association and distinguish the literary ruler from other prominent Satavahana kings.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Gathasaptasati?
o: A Paisachi grammar written in the Kuntala Satakarni period
A collection of Buddhist verses composed in Brahmi script
An anthology of 700 Maharashtri Prakrit verses dealing mainly with love, rural life and nature
A Sanskrit treatise on Jain philosophy containing 700 chapters
accepted.x: Gathasaptasati, or Sattasai, is an anthology of 700 gathas in Maharashtri Prakrit, dealing chiefly with love, rural life and nature.
accepted.tq: Identify the work through its distinctive combination of number, language and subject matter.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Gathasaptasati:
1. It is regarded as an important literary source for Satavahana society.
2. It is a reliable source for the political history of the early Satavahanas.
3. It contains descriptions of rural life and nature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Gathasaptasati is an important source for Satavahana social life and describes rural life and nature. It is not considered a source for early Satavahana political history.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded use of a source; the political-history statement reverses the source’s character.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following women are associated with contributions to Gathasaptasati?
1. Anulakshmi
2. Anupalabdha
3. Reva
4. Madhavi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Anulakshmi, Anupalabdha, Reva or Revati, and Madhavi are identified as women contributors to Gathasaptasati.
accepted.tq: Cover the complete membership of a named list rather than relying on one familiar name.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT associated with the social picture presented in Gathasaptasati?
o: Compulsory military training for all women
accepted.x: Gathasaptasati refers to sati, the absence of child marriage and the plight of wives of seafaring merchants. It does not mention compulsory military training for all women.
accepted.tq: Locate the outsider by comparing each option with the social themes attributed to the text.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the cultural information found in Gathasaptasati:
1. It refers to sugar and jaggery.
2. It mentions group dances and choral singing called Brundagana.
3. It provides evidence of house-wall paintings.
4. It refers to the hanging of criminals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four features—sugar and jaggery, Brundagana, house-wall paintings and hanging of criminals—are included in the social picture associated with Gathasaptasati.
accepted.tq: Treat each social detail as an independent statement and select the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gathasaptasati opens with a prayer addressed to
accepted.x: The work opens with a prayer to Shiva.
accepted.tq: Test the opening invocation directly, using nearby religious figures as distractors.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets contains only early Telugu or Desi words associated with Gathasaptasati?
accepted.x: Atta, Addam, Potta and Pilla are among the early Telugu words associated with Gathasaptasati. Other recorded examples include Padi, Pandi, Ammi and Tuppu.
accepted.tq: Recognise the linguistic list by separating vernacular words from technical historical terms.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work to deal with
accepted.x: Gathasaptasati is described as the first literary work covering all the Navarasas.
accepted.tq: Match the work with its distinctive literary classification rather than its language alone.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Hala is correct?
o: He wrote Katantra grammar in Sanskrit during the reign of Kuntala Satakarni.
He composed Brihatkatha in Paisachi and introduced Brahmi script.
He honoured the poets Kumarila and Sripalita and his reign is regarded as a golden age of Prakrit.
He founded the Buddhist Mahayana school at Nagarjunakonda.
accepted.x: Hala honoured Kumarila and Sripalita, and his reign is regarded as a golden age of Prakrit literature.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–achievement association and reject deeds belonging to other authors or traditions.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Satavahana-associated works:
1. Brihatkatha was written by Gunadhya in Paishachi Prakrit.
2. Katantra was a Sanskrit grammar associated with Sarvavarma.
3. Lilavati Parinayam was written by Kutuhala in Prakrit.
4. Harivijaya was written by Sarvasena in Prakrit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Brihatkatha is associated with Gunadhya, Katantra with Sarvavarma, Lilavati Parinayam with Kutuhala, and Harivijaya with Sarvasena.
accepted.tq: Verify each work through its author–language combination instead of relying on a single familiar pairing.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Brihatkatha served as the base for which of the following works?
1. Kathasaritsagara
2. Brihatkatha Manjari
3. Lilavati Parinayam
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Brihatkatha formed the basis of Kathasaritsagara by Somadeva Suri and Brihatkatha Manjari by Kshemendra. Lilavati Parinayam is a separate work associated with Kutuhala.
accepted.tq: Separate derivative works from an unrelated literary title.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Lilavati Parinayam is associated with which of the following descriptions?
o: Nagarjuna’s commentary on Prajnaparamita at Amaravati
Hala’s marriage to the Sinhala princess Lilavati near the Bhimeswara temple at Saptagodavari
Sarvavarma’s composition of a Sanskrit primer at Paithan
Gunadhya’s translation of Brihatkatha into Sanskrit
accepted.x: Lilavati Parinayam by Kutuhala concerns Hala’s marriage to the Sinhala princess Lilavati near the Bhimeswara temple at Saptagodavari, identified with Draksharamam.
accepted.tq: Use the cluster of person, event and place to identify the correct literary association.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Samayasara is a Jain philosophical work associated with Kundakundacharya. The other pairs combine unrelated authors, works or descriptions.
accepted.tq: Start with the complete three-part association of work, author and subject.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Suhrullekha and Ratnavali are associated with Acharya Nagarjuna.
2. Prajnaparamita is traditionally attributed to Acharya Nagarjuna.
3. Kamasutra and Nyayabhashya are associated with Vatsyayana.
4. Kathasaritsagara was written by Somadeva Suri.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The listed works are associated respectively with Nagarjuna, Vatsyayana and Somadeva Suri as stated.
accepted.tq: Check several author–work associations together and avoid swapping neighbouring literary names.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Yogasara is correct?
o: It is associated with Kundakundacharya, though some references attribute it to Nagarjuna.
It is the source text of Kathasaritsagara written by Somadeva Suri.
It is the Sanskrit grammar of Sarvavarma.
It was exclusively written by Sarvasena in Maharashtri Prakrit.
accepted.x: Yogasara is associated with Kundakundacharya in the cited examination key, while some references attribute it to Nagarjuna.
accepted.tq: Handle a source-attribution variation without confusing it with the authors of neighbouring works.
accepted.sec: Literature → author; Gathasaptasati as social source, women contributors  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The most common metal used in Satavahana coins was
accepted.x: Lead was the most common metal used in Satavahana coins. Potin, copper, bronze and silver were also used.
accepted.tq: Identify the dominant item in a material-composition list, not merely an item that appears in it.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Potin, used in Satavahana coinage, was an alloy of
accepted.x: Potin was a copper–tin–lead alloy used in Satavahana coinage.
accepted.tq: Test the exact composition of a technical term through element substitution traps.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Satavahana gold and silver currency:
1. The Satavahanas did not issue gold coins.
2. Roman gold coins circulated at places including Attirala, Salihundam and Vijayawada.
3. Silver coins were known as karshapanas.
4. Gold was used only as bullion according to the cited account.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Satavahanas issued no gold coins in the cited account, although Roman gold coins circulated. Silver coins were called karshapanas, and gold was used as bullion.
accepted.tq: Combine the distinction between locally issued coins, circulating foreign coins and bullion.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following places is NOT included among the locations where Roman gold coins circulated?
accepted.x: The listed locations include Attirala, Salihundam, Vijayawada, Vinukonda, Nagarjunakonda and Nellore. Kanchipuram is not included in that list.
accepted.tq: Test completeness of a geographical list by identifying the externally introduced location.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Ship-motif coins are associated with which of the following Satavahana rulers?
1. Vasishthiputra Pulumavi
2. Yajna Sri Satakarni
3. Gautamiputra Satakarni
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Ship-motif coins are associated with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni. Gautamiputra Satakarni is associated with the beginning of portrait coins, not ship coins.
accepted.tq: Separate rulers by coin motif and reject the attractive but unrelated portrait-coin association.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The ship with an anchor motif on Satavahana coins is significant primarily because it indicates
o: the conquest of inland forest regions
accepted.x: The ship motif, including the ship with an anchor, is regarded as evidence of maritime trade.
accepted.tq: Infer the economic significance of a visual coin symbol rather than memorising the symbol alone.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the issue of ship-motif coins is correct?
o: Every later Satavahana ruler issued ship-motif coins.
No later Satavahana ruler issued ship-motif coins after the rulers associated with the motif.
Ship-motif coins were issued exclusively by the Shalankayanas.
Only Gautamiputra Satakarni issued ship-motif coins.
accepted.x: The cited account associates ship-motif coins with Vasishthiputra Pulumavi and Yajna Sri Satakarni and states that no later ruler issued them.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme word “every” and distinguish the known issuers from later rulers.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Portrait coins in the Satavahana period represent
o: a Gupta innovation copied by the Satavahanas
an indigenous innovation, beginning with Gautamiputra Satakarni
a Roman practice introduced only under Yajna Sri Satakarni
a practice restricted to copper coins of Hala
accepted.x: Portrait coins are regarded as an indigenous innovation, and their issue began with Gautamiputra Satakarni. Silver portrait coins became common after him.
accepted.tq: Link the innovation, initiator and subsequent development in one precise association.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gautamiputra Satakarni is especially associated with which development in Satavahana coinage?
o: Introduction of iron coins with copper coating
Replacement of Brahmi by Kharosthi legends
Exclusive issue of Roman gold coins
accepted.x: Portrait coins began with Gautamiputra Satakarni, while silver portrait coins became common after his reign.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the ruler linked with the beginning of portrait coinage from rulers linked with ship motifs.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bilingual silver portrait coins of later Satavahana rulers carried which languages on their two sides?
accepted.x: The bilingual silver portrait coins carried Prakrit on one side and a Dravidian language on the other.
accepted.tq: Distinguish languages from scripts: Brahmi is the script, whereas Prakrit and a Dravidian language are the linguistic forms.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Satavahana coin legends?
o: They were exclusively in Tamil written in Greek script.
They were in Paisachi written in Roman script.
They were generally in Prakrit written in Brahmi script.
They were exclusively in Sanskrit written in Kharosthi script.
accepted.x: Satavahana coin legends were generally in Prakrit and written in Brahmi script.
accepted.tq: Keep language and script separate while identifying the standard form of the legends.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Rishabhadatta inscription, one gold coin was equivalent to
accepted.x: The exchange value given is 1 gold coin or suvarna equal to 35 karshapanas.
accepted.tq: Use the exact exchange ratio and choose the central value among nearby numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the terms used in the exchange account?
o: A silver coin was called a karshapana, while one suvarna was equal to 35 karshapanas.
A gold coin was called a karshapana and a silver coin a suvarna.
A silver coin was called a suvarna, while one karshapana was equal to 35 suvarnas.
Both suvarna and karshapana denoted only copper coins.
accepted.x: The silver coin was called a karshapana, and one suvarna was equivalent to 35 karshapanas.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similar monetary terms by checking denomination and exchange value.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a motif found on Satavahana coins?
accepted.x: Recorded Satavahana coin motifs include the elephant, horse, lion, camel, chaitya and dharmachakra. A trident is not included in the stated list.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd symbol by recalling the complete motif group.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ujjain symbol appearing on the reverse of Satavahana coins is represented by
o: a circle divided into eight segments
accepted.x: The Ujjain symbol is described as a cross with four circles and appears on the reverse of Satavahana coins.
accepted.tq: Translate the visual description into the correct numismatic symbol.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Satavahana coins were found in which combination of shapes?
1. Round
2. Square
3. Rectangular
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Satavahana coins occurred in round, square and rectangular forms.
accepted.tq: Select the complete set of physical forms rather than assuming all ancient coins were round.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following stages of coin production or circulation in the chronological order indicated:
A. Die-struck coins
B. Punch-marked coins
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Punch-marked coins came first, followed by die-struck coins.
accepted.tq: Fix the sequence by identifying the earlier minting method before comparing the two items.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Iron coins with a copper coating are associated with
accepted.x: Iron coins with a copper coating are attributed to the Shalankayanas, not the Satavahanas.
accepted.tq: Avoid assigning a distinctive coin type to the better-known neighbouring dynasty.
accepted.sec: Coinage - metals, ship-motif, bilingual and portrait coins  [APPSC]
